n.reason: bare letter n; SUBTLEX-NL keeps 'n (een) as its own row (rank 81), so what remains is initials, spelling and residue of 'n written without its apostrophe

t.reason: bare letter t; SUBTLEX-NL keeps 't (het) as its own row (rank 58). Most of the bare count is 't.' with the apostrophe lost in the source subtitles; the bare letter is not a Dutch word

s.reason: bare letter s; SUBTLEX-NL keeps 's as its own row (rank 316); the remainder is plural-s and 's morgens residue with the apostrophe lost

m.reason: the letter M, appearing as a clothing size or initial, not a Dutch word

mr.reason: abbreviation of meneer, not a spoken word

lk.reason: subtitle OCR misreading of ik (capital I read as lowercase l); not a Dutch word. Rank 690 in SUBTLEX-NL, 421 in FrequencyWords

exclusion_note: For the SUBTLEX-NL list (adapter subtlex-surface-frequency/v1), which keeps apostrophe words ('t, 'n, z'n, m'n) whole. Carries nl-v1's exclusions with reasons restated for the new list, and adds lk (OCR). nl-v1's verification stands: 'u' is the formal second person and is kept. Other short residue (r, d, b, c, e, dr, mrs) is left to the surface ledger's review rather than excluded on sight.
